adCopies.campaignName: Roll the Dice, Write the Wake — Celebrity Transatlantic Repositioning
adCopies.targetAudienceTag: Solo Journaling Tabletop Roleplayers: introverted writers, world-builders, and analog gamers (25–45) who invest in premium stationery, artisanal dice, and indie RPG zines, and who crave structured solitary creative time free from domestic interruption and digital noise.

variants.variantLabel: Primary Retail — Celebrity Summer Sale × Transatlantic Repositioning
variants.headline: Prompt 34 Has Been Waiting Two Months. Give It Eight Unbroken Sea Days and a Balcony with No One Else's Schedule on It.
variants.bodyCopy:
Your Thousand Year Old Vampire campaign hasn't stalled because you lost the thread. It stalled because every time you uncap the pen and reach for the oracle, someone needs a signature, a ride, a conversation, a decision — and the cognitive silence collapses before your character even makes it out of the 17th century.

A 14-night Celebrity Cruises transatlantic repositioning on an Edge-class ship is not a vacation. It's a structurally enforced writing residency that happens to cross an ocean.

Here's the math that matters: eight to ten consecutive sea days with zero port obligations, zero commute, zero domestic logistics. Your Infinite Veranda balcony — part open-air writing carrel, part teak-and-glass oracle chamber — faces nothing but deep Atlantic blue from Fort Lauderdale to the Azores. Spread the Leuchtturm flat. Line the jewel-toned polyhedrals along the rail. Roll. Write. Let the fictional cartography spill into the margins without a single interruption.

When you need a change of surface, Edge-class ships deliver exactly what a solo journaling session demands: a genuine onboard library with individual reading nooks, low-traffic indoor lounges with actual comfortable chairs and small side tables, and a ship-wide atmosphere that leans toward self-directed quiet rather than organized-fun announcements every twenty minutes. Celebrity doesn't program belly-flop contests. That's the point.

Your two or three port days — Ponta Delgada in the Azores, Funchal in Madeira, Lisbon — are atmospheric, not theme-park. Cobblestone streets, volcanic ridgelines, centuries-old bookshops. Walk off the ship, find a quiet café, roll a few oracle prompts, and write the scene where your vampire haunts a crumbling Portuguese colonial estate. The setting does half the world-building for you.

The timing is deliberate: late autumn through post-holiday winter, November 2026 to January 2027. You've just survived the full social-obligation gauntlet — Thanksgiving, office parties, holiday dinners, New Year's. A transatlantic crossing in January is a socially sanctioned disappearance. Nobody questions it. Nobody follows you.

Book during the Celebrity Summer Sale window (June 2 – July 27, 2026) and the sailing comes with bonus stateroom savings that help unlock a balcony fare — the private writing carrel that makes this entire concept work — without the solo-traveler sticker shock. You also pick up bonus onboard credit: think of it as your floating dice-and-ink fund. Specialty espressos in the library at 10 a.m. A bottle of wine delivered to the balcony at golden hour while you write your vampire's final memory. A spa appointment to unknot the hand that's been scrawling journal entries for six consecutive hours. The OBC isn't a cruise perk — it's patronage for the creative process.

Bringing a co-GM or a writing partner who respects the quiet? Their fare drops too under the same booking window.

Fourteen nights. Eight-plus sea days. One oracle. Zero interruptions. Prompt 34 doesn't stand a chance.

adPlatformTargetingHooks.demographicTargeting: Adults 25–45, skewing toward knowledge workers and creative professionals, introverted personality indicators, higher-than-average discretionary spend on stationery, analog hobbies, and independent publishing. variants.variantLabel: Aspirational Upsell — Explora Journeys All-Suite Transatlantic
variants.headline: The Oracle Doesn't Need a Bigger Table. It Needs the Whole Library to Itself.
variants.bodyCopy:
You already know the transatlantic crossing is the structurally correct move for your Thousand Year Old Vampire campaign — eight to ten consecutive sea days, no port-day interruptions, enforced cognitive silence while the Atlantic scrolls past your balcony.

But if your creative-professional income has crossed the threshold where you buy the hand-stitched leather Leuchtturm cover and the artisanal brass polyhedrals without flinching, there's a tier above the balcony writing carrel: Explora Journeys. All-suite. All-inclusive. And quiet in a way that redefines what "quiet" means on the open ocean.

Explora's ships are small-fleet, all-suite vessels designed for guests who treat their stateroom as a private study, not a place to change clothes between activities. Every suite has a generous private terrace — your oracle table with an unobstructed Atlantic horizon. The onboard atmosphere is architecturally and programmatically built around self-directed stillness: no PA announcements blaring pool-deck trivia, no mandatory-fun schedules, no crowd density that forces you to compete for a library chair. You sit down. You open the journal. You roll. Nobody materializes.

The all-inclusive structure removes every transactional interruption from your writing day. Espresso at the library nook? Included. A glass of something good delivered to your terrace at golden hour while your vampire's timeline fractures across three centuries? Included. You never break the creative trance to sign a check or calculate a bar tab. The cognitive silence extends from the page to the entire logistics layer of your day.

Book during the Explora promotional window (May 27 – June 27, 2026) on a qualifying late-autumn or winter transatlantic sailing and you pick up a Journey Credit of up to $3,500 plus up to 25% off published fares. That Journey Credit is your onboard world-building endowment — spa time for the cramped writing hand, a curated shore excursion in the Azores to walk through the volcanic landscape that's about to become your vampire's 19th-century exile, or simply banked against the all-inclusive rate to soften the premium.

This is the version of the crossing where you don't share the silence with anyone you didn't choose. Fourteen nights. An entire suite. The oracle finally gets the room it deserves.

Prompt 34 won't survive the first sea day.

Journey Credit amount and discount percentage vary by voyage, suite category, and booking date. Transatlantic or repositioning itinerary availability on Explora Journeys vessels must be confirmed at time of booking; not all routes or dates may be available in the Nov 2026 – Jan 2027 corridor. All fares are per person, suite-category dependent, and subject to availability. Explora Journeys is a luxury-tier line; pricing reflects all-suite, all-inclusive positioning and will be materially higher than standard cruise-line fares. Offer details, itinerary, and pricing subject to change without notice. Contact the booking platform to verify current sailing availability and applicable promotional savings.

SYSTEM:
You are an elite, direct-response direct-to-consumer (DTC) copywriting agent. Your sole purpose is to synthesize a hyper-targeted Creative Brief with live Inventory/Promotional data to write high-converting retail ad copy.

### INPUTS TO PROCESS:
1. {{CREATIVE_BRIEF_JSON}}: Contains the isolated niche, core question answer, insider vocabulary, visual anchor, and target audience data.
2. {{INVENTORY_MANIFEST_JSON}}: Contains the live cruise line, ship class, itinerary, dates, promotions, and critical booking window deadlines.

### STRICT AD COPY RULES:
1. THE EXPANSION RULE: Do not invent new creative concepts or change the marketing angle. Your job is strictly to expand the specific hook provided in the Creative Brief into natural, flowing copy, seamlessly embedding the pricing, promotions, and itinerary constraints.
2. HYPER-SPECIFICITY & INSIDER COGNITION: Lean heavily into the unique pain points, specific tools (e.g., exact brand names or specific rulesets mentioned), and insider vocabulary from the brief. If a regular tourist doesn't understand the opening line, but the target enthusiast feels seen, you have succeeded.
3. NO MASS-GROUP OR ISOLATED TRAVELER TRAPS: Pitch this as a self-contained retail vacation for an individual, a couple, or a single household. Do not use terms like "group cruise," "organized meetups," "clubs," or "mass gatherings." Never alienate travelers who may want to bring a spouse or partner, but keep the core focus on the personal passion.
4. BANNED TRAVEL-AGENT PLATITUDES: You are strictly forbidden from using generic industry buzzwords. Ban these words completely: "paradise", "escape", "unwind", "cruising", "hidden gem", "luxury for less", "magnificent", "breathtaking".
5. INTEGRATE THE PROMO LEGALLY & LIFESTYLE-WISE:
   - Translate generic incentives into the subculture's lifestyle (e.g., reframe Onboard Credit as a specific lifestyle subsidy matching their props/hobbies).
   - Append mandatory, clear-cut discretionary disclaimers at the bottom of the body copy regarding select sailings, stateroom dependencies, and live lookup availability to protect the platform.

### VARIANTS:
Produce a primary retail play on the strongest applicable promo, plus an aspirational upsell variant for each additional applicable promo tier when one fits. Tag each variant with the exact promo id it leans on (use "none" only if a variant features no promo). Only reference promo ids present in the inventory manifest's appliedPromos.

### OUTPUT FORMAT:
Return a single valid JSON object: campaignName, targetAudienceTag, primaryPromoApplied, and a variants array. Each variant: promoApplied, variantLabel, headline, bodyCopy, pricingDisclaimers, callToAction, adPlatformTargetingHooks {demographicTargeting, interestKeywords}. No prose outside the JSON.
